terminal.description: The page runs in the Browser panel and reloads every time you save. The shell is here if you want to look around the files.

tasks.title: Link the home page to the classes page
tasks.description:
Under Classes in `index.html`, the sentence says times and prices are on the classes page. Make the words `classes page` a link to `classes.html`.

Use a relative address: both files sit in the same folder. The check looks for a link on the home page that leads to `classes.html`, and makes sure its words say where it goes.
nextSteps: Read "The anchor element" and "Addresses: full and relative" in the lesson.
Find the sentence about the classes page under Classes.
Wrap the words that name the page in a link with the right address.
Save, click the link in the Browser panel, and press Check.
hints: A link wraps the words a visitor clicks. The address goes in an attribute on the opening tag.
Both pages are in the same folder, so the address is only the file name.
The words become `classes page`, with the other page's file name in the quotes.

tasks.title: Link back from the classes page
tasks.description:
At the top of `classes.html`, make `Back to Kilnworth Pottery` a link to the home page, `index.html`.

The check opens `classes.html` and looks for a link that leads to the home page and has words a visitor can read.
nextSteps: Find the line about going back at the top.
Wrap its words in a link to the home page.
Save and press Check. To try it, follow your first link in the Browser panel and click this one.
hints: This is the same kind of link as the first task, in the other direction.
The home page is the file the Browser panel opens first. It sits in the same folder.
Wrap the whole line in `` and ``.

tasks.title: Jump to each section
tasks.description:
Near the top of `index.html` is a line that says `Jump to: Classes, The shop, Visit us`. Make each of those words a link to its section on the same page.

- give the headings the ids `classes`, `shop` and `visit`
- link `Classes`, `The shop` and `Visit us` to them

The check looks for each id on its heading, and for a link to each one.
nextSteps: Read "Jumping within a page" in the lesson.
Add an `id` to each of the three section headings.
Wrap each word after "Jump to" in a link to its id.
Save, click each link in the Browser panel, and press Check.
hints: A link to a part of the same page has two halves: a name on the part, and a link that uses the name.
The name is an `id` attribute on the heading. The link's address is that id with one character in front.

For example `

The shop

` and `The shop`. Do the same for the other two.

tasks.title: Make the email and phone number links
tasks.description:
Under Visit us, the last line gives the studio's email address and phone number.

- clicking `hello@kilnworth.example` starts a new email to it
- tapping `01632 960418` offers to call it. The number is in the UK, so the international form starts `+44`

The text on the page stays as it is. The check looks for an email link to the studio's address and a phone link with the studio's number.
nextSteps: Read "Email and phone links" in the lesson.
Wrap the email address in a link with the scheme for email.
Wrap the phone number in a link with the scheme for calls.
hints: These are ordinary links. Only the start of the address is different.
The email scheme is a word that ends in `to:`. The phone scheme is three letters and a colon.
Use `mailto:` followed by the address, and `tel:` followed by `+44` and the number without its first 0 or any spaces.
